subject.title: feat(ui): logo-scare lobster visits; drop the model-auth-expiring chip

question: Should the Control UI remove pre-expiry provider warnings entirely, or retain a less noisy actionable notification for credentials that are still working but nearing expiry?
rationale: The patch changes a deliberate user-facing auth-health signal rather than repairing an unambiguous defect; source and screenshots do not establish the intended long-term warning policy.

options.title: Use a quieter actionable expiry signal
options.body: Retain expiry visibility with throttling, a threshold, or a non-nagging status treatment while keeping the expired-auth attention item.

options.title: Remove pre-expiry warnings
options.body: Accept that users learn about authentication trouble only when it has expired, while keeping the existing expired-auth recovery route.

options.title: Pause the auth-warning portion
options.body: Land neither the warning removal nor its related budget adjustment until an owner defines the intended provider-health UX.

recommendation.title: Use a quieter actionable expiry signal
recommendation.body: Retain expiry visibility with throttling, a threshold, or a non-nagging status treatment while keeping the expired-auth attention item.

likelyOwner.reason: Available release-history context connects this person to the original Model Auth status and attention-callout surface.
